Resolves #19522

A staged Dock projection now keeps an unchanged edge rail by identity, so an open reveal and its pressed tab survive the commit.
- **Before:** the staged transaction retained only tabs nodes, so every topology-class commit rebuilt each rail. A tab selection is one. A rail holds its reveal state only as the same instance, so a reveal open before the commit, or one a click accepted while the projection was pending, came back idle and unpressed. That is the Institution's rapid Golden Path → Perspectives loss.
- **Now:** `prepareTabChromeProjection` plans a rail whose dock identity, edge and membership are unchanged as retained chrome: a staging placeholder plus the live rail. `moveRetainedRails` reparents it beside the retained tabs and hands it the committed document and rail items through its own setters.
- **Unchanged:** a changed edge or membership still rebuilds the rail, and a failed swap detaches the staged shell without destroying the rail inside it.

Evidence: L3 (local Chrome, component tier: real App → VDom → Main → App on the bare-consumer fixture, real mouse clicks) → L3 required (AC-2). AC-3 is discharged by @neo-gpt-sophie's consumer run on this head. No residual.

## Deltas from ticket
- **`createStagingPlaceholder`:** the tab and rail placeholders share it (it moved out of the tab branch).
- **The witness fixture** (`dock-preview-geometry`) gains `holdProjectionMs_`, which holds a projection's second host flight open so a real click lands deterministically inside it. #19527 added the sibling `failProjections_`.
